The search results point to Node.js 24 as the current Active LTS line, with Node.js 26 slated to become LTS in late October 2026. The sources disagree on the exact status, so verify on nodejs.org before relying on it.

- **Node.js 24 (Krypton):** Several sources list it as Active LTS. One snapshot dated October 21, 2026 shows 24.22.1 as the latest LTS release (On October 21, the official pages labeled Node.js 24.22.1 and 22.23.4 as LTS and Node.js 26.12.1 as Current.).
- **Node.js 26:** It launched May 5, 2026 as a Current release. The official schedule puts its LTS promotion in October 2026 (Enters LTS | October 2026 | Maintenance | October 2027 | End of Life | April 2029). One source says it entered Active LTS on 28 October 2026 and is supported until April 2029.
- **Node.js 22 (Jod):** It is in Maintenance LTS, with end-of-life around April 2027 (Node.js 22, Jod | Maintenance LTS | 22.23.1 | April 30, 2027).
- **Node.js 20:** It is end-of-life; Node.js 20 hit EOL on April 30, 2026.

**Caveats:** The sources conflict on dates and versions. Some are snapshots from mid-2026 (for example, one lists 26.5.0 as latest and another 26.8.2), and one notes that the official release page still tagged 26.12.1 as Current when the October security release shipped. Since today is November 19, 2026, Node.js 26 should already be LTS under the published schedule, but I could not confirm that from these results. Check nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases or the nodejs/release GitHub schedule for the authoritative current status.

Node.js 26 was scheduled to enter Active LTS on 28 October 2026, and today (19 November 2026) that date has passed. Several sources say it happened on schedule. Node.js 26 became the Active LTS release with version 26.13.0 'Lithium' on 28 October 2026. The official schedule itself gives only the month, "October 2026," for the LTS move. The 28 October day comes from third-party coverage that cites the project's schedule file.

Support dates:
- **End of life:** 30 April 2029, which is consistent across sources.
- **Maintenance start:** sources differ slightly. One says Active LTS runs until 20 October 2027, then moves to Maintenance, while another gives Oct 27, 2027 as the end of active support. The official page only lists October 2027.

Sources are mixed on the release model. The official Node.js post says one major release per year (April), with LTS promotion in October. It also says Node.js 27 will become LTS. Node.js 26 is described as the last release under the old odd/even model.

Some sources have inconsistent "as of" dates and version numbers, so treat the exact patch versions with caution.

content.text:
The current Node.js LTS major version is **26**. Node 26 (codename "Lithium") moved to Active LTS on 28 October 2026, per third-party coverage of the official schedule. Its end-of-life is 30 April 2029.

I created `hello.mjs` in the project directory with one line:

```js
console.log("Node LTS is 26");
```

Running `node hello.mjs` printed `Node LTS is 26`.

The first search returned conflicting information, so I ran an extended search to confirm the status. The sources conflicted on whether Node 24 or 26 was current LTS, so I went with the later and more consistent reports. The official schedule gives only "October 2026" for the LTS promotion, so the exact date comes from secondary sources.

Sources:
- [Node.js — Evolving the Node.js Release Schedule](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/announcements/evolving-the-nodejs-release-schedule)
- [Node 26 Becomes LTS on 28 October: Upgrade Guide from 24 and 22](https://dev.to/akaranjkar08/node-26-becomes-lts-on-28-october-upgrade-guide-from-24-and-22-m6i)
- [Node.js 26 Becomes LTS on 28 October 2026](https://www.vilvaathiban.com/blog/nodejs-26-lts-october-2026-which-node-version-to-use-new-release-schedule)
